title: Integral blowup charts and density of the center complement
statement: Let $T$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ a nonzero quasi-coherent ideal of finite type [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $b:B=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(T)\to T$ be the ordinary glued blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup], and put $U=T\setminus V(\mathcal I)$, where $V(\mathcal I)=\{t\mid\mathcal I_t\ne\mathcal O_{T,t}\}$. Then $U$ is a nonempty dense integral open subscheme. For every nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$, the ideal $I=\Gamma(V,\mathcal I)$ is nonzero. For every choice $I=(f_0,\ldots,f_r)$, the restriction $b^{-1}(V)\to V$ identifies over $V$ with $\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal R_A(I))=\operatorname{Bl}_I(V)$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup], and is covered by the affine open subschemes $C_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A[I/f_i])$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]. These identifications respect restriction to smaller affine opens. A zero generator gives the empty chart; if $f_i\ne0$, $A[I/f_i]\subseteq A_{f_i}$ is a nonzero domain and $C_i\cap b^{-1}(U)=D_{C_i}(f_i)$ is a nonempty dense principal open. At least one such nonempty chart occurs over every nonempty $V$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-scheme-ideal-generic-stalk] to the nonzero quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$ on $T$. It gives $I=\Gamma(V,\mathcal I)\ne0$ for every nonempty affine open $V$, and $\mathcal I_\eta=\mathcal O_{T,\eta}$ at the generic point $\eta$. These are exactly clauses (a), (b), and (d) of that lemma; no Noetherian hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tag 02ND (lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme), nonzero ideal hypothesis; generic-ideal input expanded by the cited node

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine], $V(\mathcal I)$ is closed, so $U$ is open. Step 1 puts $\eta$ in $U$, making $U$ nonempty and dense, since $\overline{\{\eta\}}=T$. Finally $U$ is integral: it is nonempty, and every nonempty affine open in $U$ is also an affine open in $T$, with the same structure ring, hence a domain by [def-pc-integral-scheme].

source.place: Tag 02ND (lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme), center-complement argument; affine zero-locus description supplied by cited node

proof.text: Fix a nonempty affine $V\subseteq T$. Use the cover comparison of [prop-nagata-global-blowup-cover-independent] to include $V$ in the chosen affine cover. The gluing datum [def-nagata-global-blowup-glue-data] uses the local schemes $\mathsf B_W(\mathcal I)$ and their inverse images of $W\cap W\prime$. The gluing theorem [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] therefore embeds each local scheme as an open of $B$, with intersection exactly the prescribed overlap. The image of $\mathsf B_V(\mathcal I)$ is $b^{-1}(V)$: one containment follows from its structure map to $V$; for the other, represent $x\in b^{-1}(V)$ in any local piece $\mathsf B_W(\mathcal I)$. Since $b(x)\in W\cap V$, that representative is in the prescribed overlap with $\mathsf B_V(\mathcal I)$, hence in its image. By [def-nagata-global-blowup-local-model] and [def-nagata-affine-blowup], this gives the required isomorphism over $V$ with $\operatorname{Bl}_I(V)=\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal R_A(I))$. The argument is about the glued scheme and its open pieces, not merely a bijection of underlying sets.

source.place: Gluing, (2), and (3); equivalently Stacks divisors.tex Tag 0804 (lemma-blowing-up-affine), first assertion

proof.text: The identifications in step 3 respect smaller affine opens. Include both affine opens in the gluing cover of step 3. On a common basic affine refinement $D(s)$, [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-restrict] gives the isomorphisms $r_{i,s}$ and $r_{j,s}$ over the localized base. By [def-nagata-global-blowup-overlap-basic-map], the overlap map is $\omega_{ij,s}=r_{j,s}\circ r_{i,s}^{-1}$. Thus $\omega_{ij,s}\circ r_{i,s}=r_{j,s}$. Composing this equality with the local embeddings into $B$ shows that the two comparisons from the blowup over $D(s)$ to $B$ agree. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] makes the comparisons equal on the whole inverse image of the smaller affine open, since these basic refinements cover it. This is the required restriction compatibility; no affineness of an intersection of affine opens is assumed.

source.place: Gluing along common affine refinements; restriction maps as in prop-nagata-affine-blowup-restrict

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine](a), the finite-type hypothesis on $\mathcal I$ implies that $I=\Gamma(V,\mathcal I)$ is a finitely generated $A$-module, hence a finitely generated ideal. For any chosen generating family $I=(f_0,\ldots,f_r)$, apply [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover] to the affine blowup in step 3. It supplies the finite open cover by $C_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A[I/f_i])$ over $V$. These are the chart algebras of [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], with their canonical $A$-algebra structure. The chart isomorphism [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart] is over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, so the map from each chart to $V$ is induced by that structure map.

If $f_i=0$, then $A_{f_i}$ is the zero ring, because making $0$ invertible forces $1=0$. Its unital $A$-subalgebra $A[I/f_i]$ from [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] is therefore the zero ring. Its spectrum is empty, since the zero ring has no proper prime ideal. This proves the zero-generator clause, rather than silently omitting zero generators.

source.place: Tag 07Z3 (lemma-affine-blowup), description of the chart algebra; zero-denominator case

proof.text: If $f_i\ne0$, $A$ is a domain by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. The localization $A_{f_i}$ is a nonzero domain: $1/1=0$ would imply $f_i^n=0$ for some $n$, and $(a/f_i^m)(c/f_i^n)=0$ implies $f_i^Nac=0$, hence $a=0$ or $c=0$. The unital subalgebra $R_i=A[I/f_i]\subseteq A_{f_i}$ of [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] is consequently a nonzero domain, and the image of $f_i$ in it is nonzero by the same fraction criterion.

Write $R_i=A[I/f_i]$. In $R_i$ each generator satisfies $f_j=f_i(f_j/f_i)$, and $f_i\in I$; hence $IR_i=(f_i)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine], $U\cap V=\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(I)$. Under the chart map, a prime $\mathfrak q\subset R_i$ lies over this open exactly when its contraction to $A$ does not contain $I$, equivalently $IR_i\not\subseteq\mathfrak q$. As $IR_i=(f_i)$, this is exactly $f_i\notin\mathfrak q$. Thus, as open subschemes, $C_i\cap b^{-1}(U)=D_{C_i}(f_i)$. Here the prime contraction description is the definition of the affine spectrum map [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; the equal open subsets carry the same restricted structure sheaf.

source.place: Tag 07Z3 (lemma-affine-blowup), assertion (2), with its elementary proof written out

proof.text: For $f_i\ne0$, step 7 makes the image of $f_i$ a non-zero-divisor in $R_i$. Apply [lem-pc-principal-open-dense-of-nonzerodivisor] to obtain density of $D_{C_i}(f_i)$. This open is nonempty because the zero ideal is prime in the nonzero domain $R_i$ and does not contain $f_i$. Finally $I\ne0$ from step 1 implies some generator $f_i$ is nonzero; its chart and principal open are nonempty. This works over every nonempty affine $V$ and completes all clauses.
